title: God's speech to the ancestors and in the Son
english: So God, he says, spoke to our ancestors in various ways, each suited to its time, through the prophets who belonged to them—to Abraham, Moses, and those who came after. But now that all time was reaching its completion, he has spoken to us in the Son (Hebrews 1:2). That is, he first instructed our race through his own servants by laws suited to each generation for acquiring righteousness and the knowledge of God. Then, when the times had been completed, he announced to us in Christ and in the plan accomplished through him the complete grace of these things. By this he means the restoration of our human nature after the cross, through his resurrection, to an incorruptible and sinless state.

added_allusions.reason: Gennadius restates the content of Hebrews 1:1 clause by clause (God spoke to the ancestors in various ways through the prophets), but he replaces every distinctive word of the verse (polymeros kai polytropos, patrasin, lalesas, en tois prophetais) with synonyms (diaphoros, progonois, homilesas, dia ton propheton), so the link is a close paraphrase short of quotation or close echo. Demoted from clear on the Grok check; the Gemini check had agreed with clear, and the Grok wording evidence governs.
The clause reproduces the verse wording: lelaleken hemin en hyio, he has spoken to us in a Son (Hebrews 1:2, elalesen hemin en hyio).
